title: Playing a right-handed bass backwards after his grandfather tuned it
summary: Sherwood explains that his grandfather tuned the borrowed bass for a right-handed player, so he plays it backwards and a left-handed would-be player can use it.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: The show was in the group, it was some insurance company, you know, and they had a little show of their own, I mean, just people who worked for the company, you know, one guy to get up and sing, the other, a couple danced, and some guy, I could hear him talking to the panel, I'd like to play that bass, but I see that guy's left hand, I can't play that bass. So Jeff told him, he says, yeah, you think you can, eh? He says, you right-handed? He says, you go get that bass, you'll see. And he was surprised as hell when I gave him the bass, you know, it was tuned, he could just play for a right-hand hand, yeah, play it backwards, that's all.
Play it backwards, so he didn't have to change the bass bar and everything.

Didn't have to change a thing, it happened this way, my grandfather played all stringed instruments, you see, and when I, when this fella loaned me this bass, my grandfather came over to try to show me how to tune it, and being right-hand never occurred to him to show me, you know, he was an old gentleman at the time, and he didn't think about telling me to change the strings back, he just tuned it up and said, here it is. I just took it that way and started picking on it, see, put on a phonograph record, and I had been playing the bass horn for a while then, and I just went right on to this thing. Now let me tell those boys if anything happens the way I am, they come hollering. I told them all. Which one did you tell?
